why_this_works: This jambalaya succeeds through the building of layers of flavor, starting with browning the sausage to create fond, then sautéing the aromatic vegetables to build a flavor base. The one-pot rice technique allows the grains to absorb all the seasoned liquid and rendered fats, while the final low simmer ensures the rice cooks evenly without burning.
notes: Use Tony Chachere's seasoning specifically - no substitutes according to recipe

ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, cubed
1 (28 oz) can diced tomatoes, with juices
steps: Cook sliced sausage over medium-high heat in a 6-quart stock pot until slightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Add bell pepper, onion, celery, garlic and scallions. Cook until softened but not translucent, about 4 minutes.
Add cubed chicken breast and Worcestershire sauce. Cook just until chicken is no longer pink.
Add bay leaves, basil, oregano, sage, paprika, Tony Chachere's, salt, black pepper, tomatoes and chicken broth.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Add rice and bring back to a boil. Boil for 1 minute.
Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for at least 30 minutes. The jambalaya should be wet but not soupy.
